title: Principle transfer package
description: The testable transfer package for one registry principle, keyed by its identifier. Carries the six parts docs/VISION.md requires of a handoff to harness or metaharness, reconciled with the candidate-principle obligations in AGENTS.md. Maturity is not restated here: it stays sourced from docs/principles.json.

principle.description: The registry identifier this package belongs to.

confidence.description: VISION part 1. One graded axis per distinct thing the study can be confident about; the registry's single maturity label cannot express more than one.

mechanism.description: AGENTS.md principle lifecycle part 2: the causal or operational mechanism.

evidence.description: VISION part 2, first half. Multiple citations, so a principle whose label moves because of a study can cite that study without collapsing into one source string.

counterevidence.description: VISION part 2, second half. Known counterevidence and the trade-offs it establishes.

caveats.description: What the evidence does not establish. Every caveat travels with every projection of this principle.

repositoryPath.description: A repository-relative path, so a projector can check a quotation against its source.

evidenceKind.description: The AGENTS.md evidence vocabulary. Keeping the categories distinct is a repository rule, not a presentation choice.

claim.description: VISION part 1, first half. The normative statement, quoted rather than restated, with the file it is quoted from so a projector can refuse a quotation that has drifted from its source.

conditions.description: VISION part 3 and AGENTS.md principle lifecycle part 3: the task and risk conditions where the principle applies, where it must yield, and what it does not license.

source.description: A repository path, a repo@commit:path locator, or an external URL with its access date recorded in `accessed`.

resultHash.description: The deterministic output hash of a rerunnable artifact, where one exists.

behavior.description: VISION part 4 and AGENTS.md product handoff items 1 and 4: the behavior or interface suggested, and the smallest slice that could test it.

evaluation.description: VISION part 5 and AGENTS.md product handoff item 5: an evaluation that can detect improvement and regression, with the planted-control discipline that makes a passing evaluator meaningful.

effects.description: VISION part 6, one field per named dimension. Each states an expectation and its direction, not a measured result.

rollout.description: AGENTS.md product handoff item 6: risks, compatibility constraints, rollout conditions, and rollback.

returnPath.description: How a product outcome comes back as research input, so a rejected proposal closes rather than leaving the originating run open. See specification:research-workflow requirement 11.
